Please find and report:

1. The full source of the `rt_csr_survival` fixture (likely in tests/fixtures/). Show me exactly how it (a) writes a sentinel value to a CSR before the ROI, (b) marks the ROI begin/end, (c) reads the CSR back inside/after the ROI. Quote the actual asm/C.

2. The `tests/fixtures/Makefile` — how fixtures are built, what toolchain/march flags are used, how a new fixture gets added (is it automatic by glob, or must each be listed?).

3. How the ROI markers work in a fixture — the `slti x0, x0, 0x5A0` / `0x5A1` marker macros, or `<andesim/ROI.h>`. Where is the header/macro defined that fixtures include?

4. How `./andesim run --mode hybrid --verify <elf>` validates — what does "state-diff PASS: N fields match" mean, and where does the fixture's CSR value get compared (driver/state_diff.cpp already known). Specifically: does the fixture need to do anything special for the Andes CSR block to be compared, or does writing the CSR pre-ROI automatically flow through?

5. List ALL existing fixtures in tests/fixtures/ (just the names/families: asm, C-level rt_c_*, vplat_*).

6. Any existing fixture that already touches an Andes-specific CSR (mxstatus, uitb, jvt, pmacfg, mcountermask, mhsp_ctl, milmb, mdlmb, ucode, mpft_ctl, mclk_ctl) — grep the fixtures dir for these names and CSR addresses (0x7C4, 0x800, 0x017, 0xBC0, 0x7D1, etc.).

Be thorough — read the actual files, quote real code. I need concrete patterns to copy, not summaries. Report file paths with line numbers.

1	// rt_csr_survival.S
2	//
3	// 2-phase guard (L23 + L24): the writable M-mode CSRs round-trip across the
4	// QEMU1 -> vsim handoff. A value stashed before the ROI is readable inside it
5	// (ResumeDriver restores the CSR) and a value written inside the ROI is
6	// captured at drain (StateDrain::drain_with_passthrough re-reads it).
7	//
8	// Covered CSRs:
9	//   L23  mscratch                 -- M-mode software scratch (pure read/write)
10	//   L24  mepc, mcause, mtval, mie -- writable trap/interrupt CSRs
11	//
12	// History: this fixture predates the 2-phase redesign. It used to read the CSRs
13	// back in a `phase_c` AFTER the exit marker and exit with the index of the
14	// first mismatch -- but once the QEMU2 handback leg was removed, vsim drains and
15	// exits AT the exit marker, so phase_c never ran and the guard was silently
16	// dead. The check now lives INSIDE the ROI, where the vsim leg actually runs.
17	//
18	// Two assertion mechanisms:
19	//   1. In-ROI self-check (works in the plain e2e harness, no --verify): read
20	//      the CSR back inside the ROI and `bne` against the stashed sentinel,
21	//      held in a callee-stable GPR which the GPR restore round-trips. On a
22	//      regressed restore the values differ, so the fixture spins -- vsim never
23	//      reaches the exit marker, times out, and the harness reports a failure.
24	//      Used only for mscratch/mepc/mie, whose values round-trip exactly.
25	//   2. --verify (VERIFY=1): the differential oracle compares the drained CSRs
26	//      against a pure-QEMU run. Used for mcause (WLRL) and mtval (WARL), whose
27	//      cross-engine legalisation could differ from a chosen sentinel; the
28	//      oracle path compares engine-against-engine instead of against a literal.
29	//
30	// Not asserted: mip (its pending bits are hardware-driven, not writable via
31	// csrw on an M-only core) and the S-mode CSRs medeleg/mideleg/satp (the default
32	// engine does not implement them). See docs/andes_sim_limitations.ipynb.
33	
34	.section .text
35	.globl _start
36	_start:
37	    // Stash sentinels into the writable M-mode CSRs BEFORE the ROI (QEMU leg).
38	    // a1/a4/a5 are callee-stable GPRs the restore round-trips, so the in-ROI
39	    // reads below can compare against them.
40	    li      a1, 0xCAFEBABEDEADBEEF
41	    csrw    mscratch, a1            // L23 software scratch CSR
42	
43	    li      a4, 0x0000000080002340  // aligned (bit0=0): mepc is WARL
44	    csrw    mepc, a4                // L24
45	    li      a5, 0x0000000000000888  // MSIE|MTIE|MEIE: standard M-mode mie bits
46	    csrw    mie, a5                 // L24 (mstatus.MIE stays 0: no trap is taken)
47	
48	    // mcause (WLRL, a legal cause) + mtval (WARL): set for --verify coverage,
49	    // not in-ROI self-checked (cross-engine legalisation may differ from the
50	    // literal; the oracle compares engine-vs-engine instead).
51	    li      t1, 0x8000000000000007  // interrupt | code 7 (M timer): legal cause
52	    csrw    mcause, t1
53	    li      t1, 0x0000000080001234
54	    csrw    mtval, t1
55	
56	    slti    x0, x0, 0x5A0           // ENTER ROI -> hand off to vsim
57	
58	    // Read the round-trip CSRs back INSIDE the ROI: each must be restored.
59	    csrr    a0, mscratch
60	    bne     a0, a1, regress         // restore lost? spin -> timeout -> test FAIL
61	    csrr    a3, mepc
62	    bne     a3, a4, regress
63	    csrr    a6, mie
64	    bne     a6, a5, regress
65	
66	    li      a2, 0xBADC0FFEE0DDF00D
67	    csrw    mscratch, a2            // overwrite; drain must re-read this value
68	
69	    slti    x0, x0, 0x5A1           // EXIT ROI -> vsim drains the CSRs, exits 200
70	
71	    // Unreached on hybrid (vsim stops at the exit marker). Engine-portable
72	    // SimControl exit so the same ELF still runs to completion standalone.
73	    li      t0, 0xe0080000
74	    sw      x0, 0(t0)
75	1:  j       1b
76	
77	regress:
78	    j       regress                 // a restored CSR is wrong: hang -> harness FAIL

OBJDUMP   := $(TOOLCHAIN)/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-objdump

# Runtime sources live at the repo root (runtime/) -- they are the
# user-facing andesim runtime; fixtures are just one consumer. The linker
# script moved with them (test.ld -> runtime/andesim.ld, same content).
RUNTIME_DIR := ../../runtime
LDSCRIPT    := $(RUNTIME_DIR)/andesim.ld
# Fixture-only helpers (csr ROI markers; NOT part of the portable runtime).
HELPERS_DIR := runtime

CFLAGS  := -march=rv64gc -mabi=lp64d -nostdlib -static -Wall
LDFLAGS := -T $(LDSCRIPT) -nostdlib -static

# All fixtures share andesim.ld (load base 0x00100000, andes_ae350 DRAM).
RT_FIXTURES := rt_all_gprs rt_abi_aliases rt_sign_bits rt_pc_jump \
               rt_long_roi rt_mem_loadstore rt_unaligned_lh \
               rt_shared_mem rt_csr_survival rt_priv_smode rt_priv_umode

# Attack / breakage programs: each demonstrates a bug in the hybrid handoff.
# NOT part of the standard 'all' target (they are expected to misbehave).
# Build individually: make break_vscratch.elf   (etc.)
BREAK_FIXTURES := break_vscratch break_vscratch_top break_mcycle_write \
                  break_verify_diverge

# C-level fixtures: standard newlib stdio (printf, fputs, ...) linked
# through the shipped vplat runtime (libandesim_runtime.a) with the
# same two-flag command users type (-B build/runtime
# -specs=andesim.specs), so the suites regression-test the real
# artifact. stdio goes out the ATCUART100 UART2 and exit/file-io through
# the SimControl device at 0xe0080000, all of which both QEMU's
# andes_ae350 and vsim model. No semihosting and no libgloss anywhere:
# vplat_syscalls.o in the archive provides every stub newlib needs, so
# the same ELF runs on fast, cycle AND hybrid and a syscall inside the
# ROI works (it just adds its real cycles to the figure).
RT_C_FIXTURES    := rt_c_hello rt_c_printf rt_c_matmul rt_c_static_buf \
                    rt_c_fcsr
RT_C_V_FIXTURES  := rt_c_v_regs rt_c_v_csrs rt_c_v_matmul rt_c_v_fill
RT_C_VPLAT_FIXTURES := vplat_hello vplat_exit41 vplat_file

RUNTIME_SRCS    := $(RUNTIME_DIR)/crt0.S $(RUNTIME_DIR)/trap.S \
                   $(RUNTIME_DIR)/handler.c
VPLAT_RT_DIR := ../../build/runtime
VPLAT_RT     := $(VPLAT_RT_DIR)/libandesim_runtime.a $(VPLAT_RT_DIR)/crt0.o \
                $(VPLAT_RT_DIR)/andesim.ld $(VPLAT_RT_DIR)/andesim.specs \
                $(VPLAT_RT_DIR)/include/andesim/ROI.h
VPLAT_CFLAGS := -march=rv64gc -mabi=lp64d -O1 -Wall
# RVV-using fixtures need -march=rv64gcv; the runtime's rv64gc objects
# link cleanly into rv64gcv programs (ld unions the arch attributes).
# The crt0 already sets mstatus.VS to Initial, so V insns don't trap.
VPLAT_V_CFLAGS := -march=rv64gcv -mabi=lp64d -O1 -Wall

.PHONY: all clean dump

all: spin.elf icount_spin.elf handoff.elf handoff_exit.elf handoff_roundtrip.elf \
     $(RT_FIXTURES:%=%.elf) $(RT_C_FIXTURES:%=%.elf) \
     $(RT_C_V_FIXTURES:%=%.elf) rt_c_v_matmul_free.elf \
     $(RT_C_VPLAT_FIXTURES:%=%.elf)

# Note: handoff.elf, handoff_exit.elf, spin.elf are referenced only by the
# EXCLUDE_FROM_ALL handoff_smoke.cpp target; they still build here for
# completeness. All targets share andesim.ld at 0x00100000.

spin.elf: spin.S $(LDSCRIPT)
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c spin.S -o spin.o
	$(LD) $(LDFLAGS) spin.o -o $@

# CSR-less spin for F5 plugin-icount e2e. Linked at 0x00100000 (andesim.ld)
# so andes_ae350's MROM at 0x80000000 stays clear when loaded via -bios.
icount_spin.elf: icount_spin.S $(LDSCRIPT)
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c icount_spin.S -o icount_spin.o
	$(LD) $(LDFLAGS) icount_spin.o -o $@

handoff.elf: handoff.S $(LDSCRIPT)
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c handoff.S -o handoff.o
	$(LD) $(LDFLAGS) handoff.o -o $@

handoff_exit.elf: handoff_exit.S $(LDSCRIPT)
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c handoff_exit.S -o handoff_exit.o
	$(LD) $(LDFLAGS) handoff_exit.o -o $@

handoff_roundtrip.elf: handoff_roundtrip.S $(LDSCRIPT) semihost_exit.inc
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c handoff_roundtrip.S -o handoff_roundtrip.o
	$(LD) $(LDFLAGS) handoff_roundtrip.o -o $@

$(RT_FIXTURES:%=%.elf): %.elf: %.S $(LDSCRIPT) semihost_exit.inc
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c $< -o $*.o
	$(LD) $(LDFLAGS) $*.o -o $@

# Break fixtures: same link as RT_FIXTURES but no semihost_exit.inc dependency
# (they exit via SimControl or deliberately hang).
$(BREAK_FIXTURES:%=%.elf): %.elf: %.S $(LDSCRIPT)
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c $< -o $*.o
	$(LD) $(LDFLAGS) $*.o -o $@

# C-level fixtures: linked exactly like a user program (see VPLAT_RT
# above). rt_c_helpers.h rides -I$(HELPERS_DIR).
$(RT_C_FIXTURES:%=%.elf): %.elf: %.c $(VPLAT_RT) $(HELPERS_DIR)/rt_c_helpers.h
	$(CC) $(VPLAT_CFLAGS) -I$(HELPERS_DIR) \
	  -B $(VPLAT_RT_DIR) -specs=andesim.specs $< -o $@

# RVV-enabled fixtures: same link, different -march. Listed separately so
# changes to VPLAT_CFLAGS don't accidentally drop V.
$(RT_C_V_FIXTURES:%=%.elf): %.elf: %.c $(VPLAT_RT) $(HELPERS_DIR)/rt_c_helpers.h
	$(CC) $(VPLAT_V_CFLAGS) -I$(HELPERS_DIR) \
	  -B $(VPLAT_RT_DIR) -specs=andesim.specs $< -o $@

# vplat smoke fixtures (tests/vplat/): exercise the runtime's own
# features (exit code, file io) with no fixture helpers.
$(RT_C_VPLAT_FIXTURES:%=%.elf): %.elf: %.c $(VPLAT_RT)
	$(CC) $(VPLAT_CFLAGS) -B $(VPLAT_RT_DIR) -specs=andesim.specs $< -o $@

# One sub-make produces all five artifacts (grouped target, make >= 4.3).
$(VPLAT_RT) &: $(RUNTIME_SRCS) $(RUNTIME_DIR)/vplat_syscalls.c \
               $(RUNTIME_DIR)/andesim.ld $(RUNTIME_DIR)/andesim.specs \
               $(RUNTIME_DIR)/ROI.h
	$(MAKE) -C $(RUNTIME_DIR)

# Markerless GEMM twin (gemm_modes.md F2). Explicit rule, NOT in
# RT_C_V_FIXTURES -- the pattern rule would look for a nonexistent
# rt_c_v_matmul_free.c. Same source, same link as the marked V fixtures,
# plus -DHYBRID_MARKERLESS (drops the ROI marker HINTs).
rt_c_v_matmul_free.elf: rt_c_v_matmul.c $(VPLAT_RT) $(HELPERS_DIR)/rt_c_helpers.h
	$(CC) $(VPLAT_V_CFLAGS) -DHYBRID_MARKERLESS -I$(HELPERS_DIR) \
	  -B $(VPLAT_RT_DIR) -specs=andesim.specs rt_c_v_matmul.c -o $@

dump: spin.elf handoff.elf handoff_exit.elf
	$(OBJDUMP) -d spin.elf
	$(OBJDUMP) -d handoff.elf
	$(OBJDUMP) -d handoff_exit.elf

clean:
	rm -f spin.o spin.elf handoff.o handoff.elf handoff_exit.o handoff_exit.elf \
	      handoff_roundtrip.o handoff_roundtrip.elf \
	      $(RT_FIXTURES:%=%.o) $(RT_FIXTURES:%=%.elf) \
	      $(RT_C_FIXTURES:%=%.elf) $(RT_C_V_FIXTURES:%=%.elf) \
	      rt_c_v_matmul_free.elf $(RT_C_VPLAT_FIXTURES:%=%.elf) \
	      $(BREAK_FIXTURES:%=%.o) $(BREAK_FIXTURES:%=%.elf)

 *
 * andesim_ROI_begin()/andesim_ROI_end() delimit the region of
 * interest. On `--mode hybrid --trigger marker` the simulator switches
 * QEMU -> vsim at begin and drains at end; the reported window_cycles
 * covers exactly the span between the two markers.
 *
 * The markers are RISC-V HINT instructions (slti x0, x0, 0x5A0/0x5A1).
 * An rd=x0 instruction discards its result, so each marker is an
 * architectural NOP on every conforming core: the SAME binary runs
 * unmodified on --mode fast, --mode cycle, and real silicon.
 *
 * Cycle-attribution contract: the "memory" clobber pins memory accesses
 * across the marker but NOT register-only computation -- the compiler may
 * hoist a register-resident kernel out of the span. To keep a kernel
 * inside the measured window, anchor it through memory (read inputs /
 * write outputs inside the span) or call it as a noinline function
 * between the markers.
 */

#ifndef ANDESIM_ROI_H
#define ANDESIM_ROI_H

static inline void andesim_ROI_begin(void)
{
  __asm__ __volatile__("slti x0, x0, 0x5A0\n" ::: "memory");
}

static inline void andesim_ROI_end(void)
{
  __asm__ __volatile__("slti x0, x0, 0x5A1\n" ::: "memory");
}

1	// Wire contract between the QEMU TCG plugin and vsim. Both sides write/read
2	// `struct hybrid_state_v1` byte-for-byte through a shared file.
3	//
4	// Stability: never repurpose offsets within a published version. Add new
5	// fields by consuming bytes from `reserved`, or by introducing v2 alongside.
6	//
7	// Endianness: multi-byte fields are little-endian (native on RV64 + x86-64
8	// host). The format is not endian-portable; cross-endian use would need an
9	// explicit byte-swap path.
10	//
11	// C and C++ both compile this header.
12	
13	#ifndef HYBRID_STATE_ABI_H
14	#define HYBRID_STATE_ABI_H
15	
16	#include <stdint.h>
17	#include <stddef.h>
18	
19	#ifdef __cplusplus
20	extern "C" {
21	#endif
22	
23	#define HYBRID_STATE_MAGIC   0x42594841u  // 'AHYB' little-endian
24	// Version 3 (Andes F0): append struct hybrid_andes_csr after mmisc_ctl, which
25	// grows the struct. Version 2 (L11) widened vreg[] to 128 bytes/register.
26	// Readers reject older files loudly (all three consumers check magic + version
27	// + size) instead of mis-parsing them.
28	#define HYBRID_STATE_VERSION 3u
29	
30	#define HYBRID_FLAG_RV64  (1u << 0)
31	#define HYBRID_FLAG_FP    (1u << 1)
32	#define HYBRID_FLAG_V     (1u << 2)
33	// v3: the struct hybrid_andes_csr block carries live values (the producer ran
34	// on an Andes core that implements at least one of those CSRs). Clear means the
35	// block is all-zero and consumers skip restore/re-read/compare of it.
36	#define HYBRID_FLAG_ANDES (1u << 3)
37	
38	// VLEN upper bound, in bytes: 128 covers the supported engine range
39	// VLEN 128..1024 (L11; also QEMU's RV_VLEN_MAX). This is the wire-format
40	// span per vector register; the LIVE width is the runtime `vlenb` field
41	// below, so one struct layout serves every engine config and the legs
42	// never disagree on offsets. A producer whose vlenb exceeds this ceiling
43	// must refuse to drain (see hybrid_v_drain_policy) rather than truncate.
44	#define HYBRID_VLEN_BYTES_MAX 128
45	
46	// L26: bytes reserved for the V-register transport scratch page -- 32 vector
47	// registers at the wire-format span. The driver maps this many bytes ABOVE
48	// the program's --mem-size (so the scratch sits past the program's RAM), and
49	// vsim's v_scratch_gpa() / kVScratchBytes use the same count. Shared here so
50	// the producer (driver mmap sizing) and consumer (vsim sweep) never disagree.
51	#define HYBRID_V_SCRATCH_BYTES (32 * HYBRID_VLEN_BYTES_MAX)
52	
53	// 64 PMP entries; pmpcfg slots reserved at 16 so the layout works for both
54	// RV64 (8 entries/CSR) and a future RV32 (4 entries/CSR) packing.
55	#define HYBRID_PMP_CFG_NUM  16
56	#define HYBRID_PMP_ADDR_NUM 64
57	
58	// v3 Andes CSR block. PMA is 16 entries: pmacfg packs them at one byte each, so
59	// on RV64 only the even-numbered cfg CSRs exist -- 16 entries live in pmacfg0
60	// (0xBC0) + pmacfg2 (0xBC2), hence 2 cfg slots; 16 pmaaddr (0xBD0..0xBDF).
61	#define HYBRID_PMA_CFG_NUM  2
62	#define HYBRID_PMA_ADDR_NUM 16
63	#define HYBRID_PMA_CFG0_CSR   0xBC0
64	#define HYBRID_PMA_ADDR0_CSR  0xBD0
65	
66	// Single source of truth for the SCALAR Andes CSRs transported in v3: X(field,
67	// csr_addr, gdb_name). Every consumer (QEMU plugin drain, ResumeDriver restore,
68	// StateDrain re-read, driver state_diff verify) iterates this list, so adding a
69	// CSR is one line here -- no consumer edits drift out of sync. PMA (arrays) is
70	// transported separately, mirroring the existing PMP loops. Each field is a
71	// 64-bit CSR value; 0 means the producing engine did not implement it (a
72	// tolerant no-op on restore). Order fixes the struct layout -- append only.
73	#define HYBRID_ANDES_CSR_LIST(X)            \
74	  X(mxstatus,       0x7C4, "mxstatus")      \
75	  X(mpft_ctl,       0x7C5, "mpft_ctl")      \
76	  X(mclk_ctl,       0x7DF, "mclk_ctl")      \
77	  X(milmb,          0x7C0, "milmb")         \
78	  X(mdlmb,          0x7C1, "mdlmb")         \
79	  X(mecc_code,      0x7C2, "mecc_code")     \
80	  X(mhsp_ctl,       0x7C6, "mhsp_ctl")      \
81	  X(msp_bound,      0x7C7, "msp_bound")     \
82	  X(msp_base,       0x7C8, "msp_base")      \
83	  X(mcountermask_m, 0x7D1, "mcountermask_m")\
84	  X(uitb,           0x800, "uitb")          \
85	  X(jvt,            0x017, "jvt")           \
86	  X(ucode,          0x801, "ucode")
87	
88	// The Andes V5 machine/user CSRs a bare-metal Andes core sets up before the ROI
89	// (boot-static memory system + extension config) plus the DSP overflow flag.
90	// Restored at resume, re-read at drain, and verified -- live only when
91	// HYBRID_FLAG_ANDES is set. 13 scalar fields (above) + PMA = 31 * uint64_t.
92	struct hybrid_andes_csr {
93	#define HYBRID_ANDES_FIELD(field, addr, name) uint64_t field;
94	  HYBRID_ANDES_CSR_LIST(HYBRID_ANDES_FIELD)
95	#undef HYBRID_ANDES_FIELD
96	  uint64_t pmacfg[HYBRID_PMA_CFG_NUM];
97	  uint64_t pmaaddr[HYBRID_PMA_ADDR_NUM];
98	};
99	
100	// All fields are naturally 8-byte aligned, so __attribute__((packed)) is
101	// unnecessary and would force unaligned access codegen. Layout is locked by
102	// the static_asserts in state_abi_check.h.
103	struct hybrid_state_v1 {
104	  uint32_t magic;
105	  uint32_t version;
106	  uint32_t flags;
107	  uint32_t hart_id;
108	  uint64_t pc;
109	  uint64_t priv;  // 0=U, 1=S, 3=M
110	
111	  uint64_t gpr[32];
112	  uint64_t fpr[32];
113	
114	  uint64_t mstatus;
115	  uint64_t mepc;
116	  uint64_t mtvec;
117	  uint64_t mcause;
118	  uint64_t mtval;
119	  uint64_t mscratch;
120	  uint64_t medeleg;
121	  uint64_t mideleg;
122	  uint64_t mip;
123	  uint64_t mie;
124	  uint64_t mcycle;
125	  uint64_t minstret;
126	  uint64_t satp;
127	
128	  uint64_t pmpcfg[HYBRID_PMP_CFG_NUM];
129	  uint64_t pmpaddr[HYBRID_PMP_ADDR_NUM];
130	
131	  uint64_t vstart;
132	  uint64_t vtype;
133	  uint64_t vl;
134	  uint64_t vlenb;
135	  uint8_t  vreg[32 * HYBRID_VLEN_BYTES_MAX];
136	  uint64_t vxsat;
137	  uint64_t vxrm;
138	  uint64_t vcsr;
139	
140	  // L20: FP control/status -- frm[7:5] | fflags[4:0], live when
141	  // HYBRID_FLAG_FP is set. Drained by the plugin, restored by ResumeDriver,
142	  // re-read by StateDrain. Pre-L20 state files carry 0 here (reserved bytes
143	  // are written as zero), which reads back as the reset value (RNE, no
144	  // flags) -- exactly the old behavior, so no version bump.
145	  uint64_t fcsr;
146	
147	  // Andes machine-setup CSRs: mcache_ctl (0x7CA) enables the L1 I/D caches,
148	  // mmisc_ctl (0x7D0) holds misc machine config. crt0 writes them once at
149	  // boot; transporting them keeps the cycle engine from resuming caches-off
150	  // (ResumeDriver has the full rationale). Drained by the plugin, restored by
151	  // ResumeDriver, but NOT re-read by StateDrain: they are boot-static and the
152	  // drained value is unused (no QEMU2 leg). Old state files carry 0 here
153	  // (reset value), which is the pre-existing behavior, so no version bump.
154	  uint64_t mcache_ctl;
155	  uint64_t mmisc_ctl;
156	
157	  // v3: Andes V5 CSR block (live when HYBRID_FLAG_ANDES). 31 * 8 = 248 bytes.
158	  struct hybrid_andes_csr andes;
159	
160	  uint8_t  reserved[64];  // zero-initialise on write; v3-compatible growth room
161	};
162	
163	#ifdef __cplusplus
164	}  // extern "C"
165	#endif
166	
167	#include "hybrid/state_abi_check.h"
168	
169	#endif  // HYBRID_STATE_ABI_H

2	 * handoff (L20).
3	 *
4	 * Phase 1 (QEMU1): set fcsr = 0x21 (frm=RTZ(1)<<5 | fflags=NX) right
5	 *   before the enter marker; the plugin drains it into
6	 *   hybrid_state_v1.fcsr (offset 5456, locked by state_abi_check.h).
7	 * Phase 2 (vsim): ResumeDriver must restore fcsr before the ROI runs.
8	 *   The in-ROI self-check reads it back; on mismatch the fixture exits 1
9	 *   immediately, so the vsim leg returns 1 instead of 200 and the harness
10	 *   fails loudly. On success it writes the distinct sentinel 0x45
11	 *   (frm=RDN(2)<<5 | fflags=NX|UF) for StateDrain to capture at the exit
12	 *   marker -- the drained file's fcsr field must read 0x45
13	 *   (tests/hybrid/e2e_fcsr_roundtrip.sh asserts both file values).
14	 *
15	 * crt0.S sets mstatus.FS=Initial, so fcsr is writable in M-mode on both
16	 * engines. The insns after the exit marker (main's epilogue) touch no FP
17	 * state, so the drain's 0-3 insn halt slack cannot disturb the sentinel.
18	 */

20	
21	#include "runtime/rt_c_helpers.h"
22	
23	int main(void)
24	{
25	  /* Phase 1 (QEMU1): non-default rounding mode + a sticky flag. */
26	  unsigned long set = 0x21; /* frm=RTZ | fflags=NX */
27	  asm volatile("csrw fcsr, %0" ::"r"(set));
28	
29	  enter_vsim();
30	
31	  /* Phase 2 (vsim): the restored fcsr must be intact. */
32	  unsigned long got;

3	 *
4	 * Configures vxsat, vxrm, vstart, vtype, and vl in the vsim ROI, then

10	 *   - vsetvli: vl=8, vtype=e32/m1/ta/ma (0xD0)

2	 *
3	 * Syscalls: all C-level fixtures link the vplat runtime
4	 * (build/runtime/libandesim_runtime.a, no semihosting): newlib stdio
5	 * bottoms out in the ATCUART100 UART2 and exit/file-io in the SimControl
6	 * device, which BOTH engines model. A syscall inside the
7	 * enter_vsim()/exit_vsim() span therefore works on vsim too -- it just
8	 * adds its real cycles (UART polling, dcache flush) to the measured
9	 * figure, so cycle-measuring fixtures keep the span syscall-free by
10	 * choice, not by rule.
11	 */
12	
13	#ifndef RT_C_HELPERS_H
14	#define RT_C_HELPERS_H
15

17	 * `slti x0, x0, 0x5A0` (ENTER) / `slti x0, x0, 0x5A1` (EXIT). Match
18	 * insn_match.h. rd=x0 makes each marker an architectural NOP, so marked
19	 * binaries also run standalone on every engine.
20	 *
21	 * marker mode pattern-matches the HINT insns directly; the helpers do not
22	 * export any `_hybrid_*_pc` symbol. PC-trigger callers pass the switch PCs
23	 * explicitly via `--pc-start`/`--pc-end` (or the env-var pair
24	 * `ROI_START`/`ROI_END`); see tests/lib/roi.sh. */
25	/* The "memory" clobber forces the compiler to spill all globals to memory
26	 * across the marker and reload them after, since vsim's drain+resume is
27	 * (from the compiler's POV) an opaque event that could observe or alter
28	 * any memory. Without it, the compiler may hoist global-pointer arithmetic
29	 * (e.g. &_impure_ptr) into a callee-saved register across the marker and
30	 * use it after resume; if vsim doesn't faithfully restore that register
31	 * the post-resume code dereferences garbage. The clobber list deliberately
32	 * does NOT include GPRs: the round-trip is required to preserve them. */

37	 * in vector registers across the boundary can be hoisted before enter_vsim
38	 * or sunk after exit_vsim, charging its cycles to the wrong phase. (Tested
39	 * on the Andes GCC at -O2/-O3: an out-of-line marker does NOT help -- a
40	 * call only forces a register spill, not the position of the compute that
41	 * consumes the value.)
42	 *
43	 * To keep a kernel inside the measured window, anchor it through memory:
44	 *   - read its inputs from memory and write its outputs to memory INSIDE
45	 *     the span (the load cannot move before enter, the store cannot move
46	 *     after exit, and the compute is data-chained between them), or
47	 *   - put the kernel in its own __attribute__((noinline)) function called
48	 *     between the markers.
49	 * Both keep every kernel op in the ROI with zero annotation and zero
50	 * overhead. Carrying live vector values in registers across the boundary is
51	 * fine for CORRECTNESS (all regs round-trip) -- rt_c_v_regs.c does exactly
52	 * that (relying on the compiler keeping x in a V register across the
53	 * boundary) as the V-regfile TRANSPORT test -- but it is not safe for cycle
54	 * attribution. */
55	static inline void enter_vsim(void)
56	{
57	  __asm__ __volatile__("slti x0, x0, 0x5A0\n" ::: "memory");
58	}
59	static inline void exit_vsim(void)
60	{
61	  __asm__ __volatile__("slti x0, x0, 0x5A1\n" ::: "memory");
62	}
63	
64	/* A pure compiler memory barrier (emits no instructions): forces pending
65	 * memory writes to complete and bars reordering across it. enter_vsim /
66	 * exit_vsim already carry this clobber on their marker insn, so the markers
67	 * anchor a kernel's output stores; markerless builds (-DHYBRID_MARKERLESS)
68	 * call roi_anchor() to pin those stores instead. */
69	static inline void roi_anchor(void)
70	{
71	  __asm__ __volatile__("" ::: "memory");
72	}
73	
74	#endif /* RT_C_HELPERS_H */

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# End-to-end harness: QEMU 1 + plugin -> vsim (2-phase, no QEMU2 handback).
3	#
4	# Memory between QEMU and vsim is shared via an /dev/shm-backed mmap
5	# (128 MB). Works for both asm fixtures (handoff_roundtrip, rt_*) and
6	# C-level fixtures (rt_c_*). C fixtures require shared mmap so the
7	# stack/heap survives handoffs; asm fixtures don't need it but run
8	# fine with it.
9	#
10	# Env:
11	#   FIXTURE         REQUIRED. .elf name under tests/fixtures/ (no .elf suffix).
12	#   TRIGGER_MODE    marker | pc (default marker).
13	#   ROI_START       pc mode switch-in PC: a 0x address or a symbol in
14	#                   $VSIM_ELF. If BOTH ROI_START and ROI_END are unset, they
15	#                   are auto-derived from the fixture's ROI marker HINTs via
16	#                   objdump (see roi_markers_from_disasm) -- the bulk runner
17	#                   relies on this; ./andesim run always passes them explicitly.
18	#   ROI_END         pc mode switch-out PC, same forms / same auto-derivation.
19	#   TIMEOUT         vsim leg timeout in seconds (default 60).
20	#   CHECK_MCYCLE_MONOTONIC=1   assert mcycle/minstret strictly increased
21	#                              between QEMU 1's drain and vsim's drain.
22	#   CHECK_PRIV=<0|1|3>         assert both drained state files carry this
23	#                              privilege (L6: 0=U, 1=S, 3=M).
24	#   VSIM_BIN, VSIM_QEMU, VSIM_PLUGIN, VSIM_ELF, NM  override built paths.
25	#   QEMU_CPU        -cpu argument for both QEMU legs (default
26	#                   andes-ax45mpv,vlen=512, pairing the default vsim
27	#                   engine). Override together with VSIM_BIN to run a
28	#                   fixture on another engine, e.g. the S/U-capable
29	#                   ax66_makatau for the rt_priv_* fixtures (the default
30	#                   ax45mpv_premium RTL is M-mode-only).
31	
32	set -euo pipefail
33	
34	SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
35	. "$SCRIPT_DIR/lib/paths.sh"
36	. "$SCRIPT_DIR/lib/roi.sh"
37	
38	FIXTURE="${FIXTURE:?FIXTURE env var is required (e.g. FIXTURE=rt_c_hello)}"
39	TIMEOUT="${TIMEOUT:-60}"
40	TRIGGER_MODE="${TRIGGER_MODE:-marker}"
41	QEMU_CPU="${QEMU_CPU:-andes-ax45mpv,vlen=512}"
42	
43	hybrid_resolve_paths
44	
45	NM="${NM:-${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN:+$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-nm}}"
46	NM="${NM:-riscv64-unknown-elf-nm}"
47	
48	case "$TRIGGER_MODE" in
49	  marker) ;;
50	  pc)
51	    if ! command -v "$NM" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
52	      echo "skip[$FIXTURE pc]: nm not found at $NM"
53	      exit 77
54	    fi
55	    # ROI_START / ROI_END name the two switch PCs (0x address or symbol in
56	    # $VSIM_ELF). ./andesim run always passes them explicitly. When a caller
57	    # leaves BOTH unset (e.g. the bulk runner scripts/run_e2e.sh), derive them
58	    # from the fixture's ROI marker HINTs via objdump, so pc mode needs no
59	    # per-fixture config and no planted boundary symbols. A partial set or a
60	    # derivation miss falls through to roi_resolve_pair's required-vars error.
61	    if [ -z "${ROI_START:-}" ] && [ -z "${ROI_END:-}" ]; then
62	      OBJDUMP="${OBJDUMP:-${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN:+$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-objdump}}"
63	      OBJDUMP="${OBJDUMP:-riscv64-unknown-elf-objdump}"
64	      if command -v "$OBJDUMP" >/dev/null 2>&1 \
65	         && MARKERS=$(roi_markers_from_disasm "$("$OBJDUMP" -d "$VSIM_ELF")"); then
66	        ROI_START="0x${MARKERS%% *}"
67	        ROI_END="0x${MARKERS##* }"
68	        export ROI_START ROI_END
69	      fi
70	    fi
71	    NM_OUT=$("$NM" --defined-only "$VSIM_ELF")
72	    roi_resolve_pair "$NM_OUT" "$FIXTURE pc" || exit 1
73	    ;;
74	  *)
75	    echo "FAIL[$FIXTURE]: unknown TRIGGER_MODE=$TRIGGER_MODE (use marker|pc)"
76	    exit 1
77	    ;;
78	esac
79	
80	# 128 MB program RAM matches the QEMU virt machine default. L26/F2: the
81	# physical mmap reserves one V-scratch page (HYBRID_V_SCRATCH_BYTES =
82	# 32 * HYBRID_VLEN_BYTES_MAX) ABOVE the program's RAM, so the V-transport
83	# scratch (vsim parks it at the mmap top page) sits past anything the program
84	# can address. Mirrors the andesim driver (shm.cpp physical_mmap_bytes).
85	# Read HYBRID_VLEN_BYTES_MAX from the shared ABI so this tracks the header
86	# (the ceiling moved 64 -> 128 once already) instead of hardcoding it.
87	VLEN_BYTES_MAX=$(awk '/^#define HYBRID_VLEN_BYTES_MAX/ {print $3}' \
88	  "$SCRIPT_DIR/../include/hybrid/state_abi.h")
89	[ -n "$VLEN_BYTES_MAX" ] || { echo "e2e: cannot read HYBRID_VLEN_BYTES_MAX from state_abi.h" >&2; exit 1; }
90	PROGRAM_SIZE=$((128 * 1024 * 1024))
91	V_SCRATCH_BYTES=$((32 * VLEN_BYTES_MAX))
92	SHARED_SIZE=$((PROGRAM_SIZE + V_SCRATCH_BYTES))
93	SHARED_MEM=$(mktemp -p /dev/shm vsim-e2e-shared.XXXXXX)
94	STATE_QEMU=$(mktemp)
95	STATE_VSIM=$(mktemp)
96	SIM_LOG=$(mktemp)
97	trap 'rm -f "$SHARED_MEM" "$STATE_QEMU" "$STATE_VSIM" "$SIM_LOG"' EXIT
98	truncate -s "$SHARED_SIZE" "$SHARED_MEM"
99	
100	PLUGIN_ARGS="outfile=$STATE_QEMU"
101	VSIM_TRIG_ARGS=()
102	if [ "$TRIGGER_MODE" = "pc" ]; then
103	  PLUGIN_ARGS="$PLUGIN_ARGS,enter_pc=0x$ENTER_PC"
104	  VSIM_TRIG_ARGS=(--hybrid-exit-pc "0x$EXIT_PC")
105	fi
106	
107	# Optional ROI kanata logging: hsim sets KANATA_FILE (and optionally
108	# OBJDUMP_FILE) when the user passes --kanata. vsim's --kanata-roi auto-
109	# derives the window from the resume PC and the unique exit PC.
110	VSIM_KANATA_ARGS=()
111	if [ -n "${KANATA_FILE:-}" ]; then
112	  VSIM_KANATA_ARGS+=(--kanata "$KANATA_FILE" --kanata-roi)
113	  if [ -n "${OBJDUMP_FILE:-}" ]; then
114	    VSIM_KANATA_ARGS+=(--objdump "$OBJDUMP_FILE")
115	  fi
116	fi
117	
118	echo "[$FIXTURE 1/2 mode=$TRIGGER_MODE] QEMU 1: drain entry state"
119	set +e
120	"$VSIM_QEMU" \
121	  -object "memory-backend-file,id=mem,share=on,mem-path=$SHARED_MEM,size=$SHARED_SIZE" \
122	  -machine andes_ae350,memory-backend=mem \
123	  -cpu "$QEMU_CPU" \
124	  -nographic \
125	  -semihosting-config enable=on,target=native \
126	  -bios "$VSIM_ELF" \
127	  -plugin "$VSIM_PLUGIN,$PLUGIN_ARGS" </dev/null >/dev/null 2>&1
128	QEMU1_RC=$?
129	set -e
130	
131	if [ "$QEMU1_RC" -ne 200 ]; then
132	  echo "FAIL[$FIXTURE]: QEMU 1 expected exit 200 on drain, got $QEMU1_RC"
133	  exit 1
134	fi
135	
136	if [ ! -s "$STATE_QEMU" ]; then
137	  echo "FAIL[$FIXTURE]: QEMU 1 did not produce state"
138	  exit 1
139	fi
140	
141	echo "[$FIXTURE 2/2 mode=$TRIGGER_MODE] vsim: resume + drain"
142	set +e
143	timeout "$TIMEOUT" "$VSIM_BIN" "$VSIM_ELF" \
144	  --resume-from-qemu "$STATE_QEMU" \
145	  --handoff-out "$STATE_VSIM" \
146	  --shared-mem-path "$SHARED_MEM" \
147	  --shared-mem-size "$SHARED_SIZE" \
148	  --shared-mem-base 0x00000000 \
149	  "${VSIM_TRIG_ARGS[@]}" \
150	  "${VSIM_KANATA_ARGS[@]}" </dev/null >"$SIM_LOG" 2>&1
151	VSIM_RC=$?
152	set -e
153	
154	# vsim drained on the exit trigger and exited 200 (kExitHandoffToQemu).
155	# Anything else is a hard failure: the cycle figure is only valid when vsim
156	# drained cleanly.
157	if [ "$VSIM_RC" -ne 200 ]; then
158	  echo "FAIL[$FIXTURE]: vsim expected exit 200 (drain), got $VSIM_RC"
159	  echo "--- sim log ---"
160	  cat "$SIM_LOG"
161	  exit 1
162	fi
163	
164	# Kernel cycles (always) + opt-in monotonic check. Offsets locked by
165	# state_abi_check.h (mcycle@624, minstret@632). vsim restores mcycle from
166	# QEMU 1's drain then counts real clock cycles, so vsim_mcycle - qemu1_mcycle
167	# is the measured region's cycle count. Runs before the RC gate so the
168	# verdict is independent of any downstream-phase failure.
169	read_u64_le() { od -A n -j "$1" -N 8 -t u8 "$2" | tr -d ' \n'; }
170	if [ -s "$STATE_VSIM" ] && [ -s "$STATE_QEMU" ]; then
171	  Q1_MCYCLE=$(read_u64_le 624 "$STATE_QEMU")
172	  Q1_MINST=$(read_u64_le  632 "$STATE_QEMU")
173	  V_MCYCLE=$(read_u64_le  624 "$STATE_VSIM")
174	  V_MINST=$(read_u64_le   632 "$STATE_VSIM")
175	  echo "[$FIXTURE kernel_cycles] $((V_MCYCLE - Q1_MCYCLE))  (vsim mcycle=$V_MCYCLE - qemu1 mcycle=$Q1_MCYCLE)"
176	  # L6: privilege survives the handoff. priv@24 locked by state_abi_check.h.
177	  if [ -n "${CHECK_PRIV:-}" ]; then
178	    Q1_PRIV=$(read_u64_le 24 "$STATE_QEMU")
179	    V_PRIV=$(read_u64_le  24 "$STATE_VSIM")
180	    echo "[$FIXTURE priv] qemu1=$Q1_PRIV vsim=$V_PRIV expected=$CHECK_PRIV"
181	    if [ "$Q1_PRIV" != "$CHECK_PRIV" ] || [ "$V_PRIV" != "$CHECK_PRIV" ]; then
182	      echo "FAIL[$FIXTURE]: drained priv mismatch (expected $CHECK_PRIV)"
183	      exit 1
184	    fi
185	  fi
186	  if [ "${CHECK_MCYCLE_MONOTONIC:-0}" = "1" ]; then
187	    echo "[$FIXTURE mcycle/minstret] qemu1: mcycle=$Q1_MCYCLE minstret=$Q1_MINST"
188	    echo "[$FIXTURE mcycle/minstret] vsim:  mcycle=$V_MCYCLE minstret=$V_MINST"
189	    if [ "$V_MCYCLE" -le "$Q1_MCYCLE" ]; then
190	      echo "FAIL[$FIXTURE]: mcycle not strictly increasing across vsim"
191	      exit 1
192	    fi
193	    if [ "$V_MINST" -le "$Q1_MINST" ]; then
194	      echo "FAIL[$FIXTURE]: minstret not strictly increasing across vsim"
195	      exit 1
196	    fi
197	    echo "[$FIXTURE mcycle/minstret] PASS: strictly increasing"
198	  fi
199	fi

#   TRIGGER_MODE    marker | pc (default marker).
#   ROI_START       pc mode switch-in PC: a 0x address or a symbol in
#                   $VSIM_ELF. If BOTH ROI_START and ROI_END are unset, they
#                   are auto-derived from the fixture's ROI marker HINTs via
#                   objdump (see roi_markers_from_disasm) -- the bulk runner
#                   relies on this; ./andesim run always passes them explicitly.
#   ROI_END         pc mode switch-out PC, same forms / same auto-derivation.
#   TIMEOUT         vsim leg timeout in seconds (default 60).
#   CHECK_MCYCLE_MONOTONIC=1   assert mcycle/minstret strictly increased
#                              between QEMU 1's drain and vsim's drain.
#   CHECK_PRIV=<0|1|3>         assert both drained state files carry this
#                              privilege (L6: 0=U, 1=S, 3=M).
#   VSIM_BIN, VSIM_QEMU, VSIM_PLUGIN, VSIM_ELF, NM  override built paths.
#   QEMU_CPU        -cpu argument for both QEMU legs (default
#                   andes-ax45mpv,vlen=512, pairing the default vsim
#                   engine). Override together with VSIM_BIN to run a
#                   fixture on another engine, e.g. the S/U-capable
#                   ax66_makatau for the rt_priv_* fixtures (the default
#                   ax45mpv_premium RTL is M-mode-only).

set -euo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/lib/paths.sh"
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/lib/roi.sh"

FIXTURE="${FIXTURE:?FIXTURE env var is required (e.g. FIXTURE=rt_c_hello)}"
TIMEOUT="${TIMEOUT:-60}"
TRIGGER_MODE="${TRIGGER_MODE:-marker}"
QEMU_CPU="${QEMU_CPU:-andes-ax45mpv,vlen=512}"

hybrid_resolve_paths

NM="${NM:-${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN:+$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-nm}}"
NM="${NM:-riscv64-unknown-elf-nm}"

case "$TRIGGER_MODE" in
  marker) ;;
  pc)
    if ! command -v "$NM" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
      echo "skip[$FIXTURE pc]: nm not found at $NM"
      exit 77
    fi
    # ROI_START / ROI_END name the two switch PCs (0x address or symbol in
    # $VSIM_ELF). ./andesim run always passes them explicitly. When a caller
    # leaves BOTH unset (e.g. the bulk runner scripts/run_e2e.sh), derive them
    # from the fixture's ROI marker HINTs via objdump, so pc mode needs no
    # per-fixture config and no planted boundary symbols. A partial set or a
    # derivation miss falls through to roi_resolve_pair's required-vars error.
    if [ -z "${ROI_START:-}" ] && [ -z "${ROI_END:-}" ]; then
      OBJDUMP="${OBJDUMP:-${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN:+$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-objdump}}"
      OBJDUMP="${OBJDUMP:-riscv64-unknown-elf-objdump}"
      if command -v "$OBJDUMP" >/dev/null 2>&1 \
         && MARKERS=$(roi_markers_from_disasm "$("$OBJDUMP" -d "$VSIM_ELF")"); then
        ROI_START="0x${MARKERS%% *}"
        ROI_END="0x${MARKERS##* }"
        export ROI_START ROI_END
      fi
    fi
    NM_OUT=$("$NM" --defined-only "$VSIM_ELF")
    roi_resolve_pair "$NM_OUT" "$FIXTURE pc" || exit 1
    ;;
  *)
    echo "FAIL[$FIXTURE]: unknown TRIGGER_MODE=$TRIGGER_MODE (use marker|pc)"
    exit 1
    ;;
esac

# 128 MB program RAM matches the QEMU virt machine default. L26/F2: the
# physical mmap reserves one V-scratch page (HYBRID_V_SCRATCH_BYTES =
# 32 * HYBRID_VLEN_BYTES_MAX) ABOVE the program's RAM, so the V-transport
# scratch (vsim parks it at the mmap top page) sits past anything the program
# can address. Mirrors the andesim driver (shm.cpp physical_mmap_bytes).
# Read HYBRID_VLEN_BYTES_MAX from the shared ABI so this tracks the header
# (the ceiling moved 64 -> 128 once already) instead of hardcoding it.
VLEN_BYTES_MAX=$(awk '/^#define HYBRID_VLEN_BYTES_MAX/ {print $3}' \
  "$SCRIPT_DIR/../include/hybrid/state_abi.h")
[ -n "$VLEN_BYTES_MAX" ] || { echo "e2e: cannot read HYBRID_VLEN_BYTES_MAX from state_abi.h" >&2; exit 1; }
PROGRAM_SIZE=$((128 * 1024 * 1024))
V_SCRATCH_BYTES=$((32 * VLEN_BYTES_MAX))
SHARED_SIZE=$((PROGRAM_SIZE + V_SCRATCH_BYTES))
SHARED_MEM=$(mktemp -p /dev/shm vsim-e2e-shared.XXXXXX)
STATE_QEMU=$(mktemp)
STATE_VSIM=$(mktemp)
SIM_LOG=$(mktemp)
trap 'rm -f "$SHARED_MEM" "$STATE_QEMU" "$STATE_VSIM" "$SIM_LOG"' EXIT
truncate -s "$SHARED_SIZE" "$SHARED_MEM"

PLUGIN_ARGS="outfile=$STATE_QEMU"
VSIM_TRIG_ARGS=()
if [ "$TRIGGER_MODE" = "pc" ]; then
  PLUGIN_ARGS="$PLUGIN_ARGS,enter_pc=0x$ENTER_PC"
  VSIM_TRIG_ARGS=(--hybrid-exit-pc "0x$EXIT_PC")
fi

# Optional ROI kanata logging: hsim sets KANATA_FILE (and optionally
# OBJDUMP_FILE) when the user passes --kanata. vsim's --kanata-roi auto-
# derives the window from the resume PC and the unique exit PC.
VSIM_KANATA_ARGS=()
if [ -n "${KANATA_FILE:-}" ]; then
  VSIM_KANATA_ARGS+=(--kanata "$KANATA_FILE" --kanata-roi)
  if [ -n "${OBJDUMP_FILE:-}" ]; then
    VSIM_KANATA_ARGS+=(--objdump "$OBJDUMP_FILE")
  fi
fi

echo "[$FIXTURE 1/2 mode=$TRIGGER_MODE] QEMU 1: drain entry state"
set +e
"$VSIM_QEMU" \
  -object "memory-backend-file,id=mem,share=on,mem-path=$SHARED_MEM,size=$SHARED_SIZE" \
  -machine andes_ae350,memory-backend=mem \
  -cpu "$QEMU_CPU" \
  -nographic \
  -semihosting-config enable=on,target=native \
  -bios "$VSIM_ELF" \
  -plugin "$VSIM_PLUGIN,$PLUGIN_ARGS" </dev/null >/dev/null 2>&1
QEMU1_RC=$?
set -e

if [ "$QEMU1_RC" -ne 200 ]; then
  echo "FAIL[$FIXTURE]: QEMU 1 expected exit 200 on drain, got $QEMU1_RC"
  exit 1
fi

if [ ! -s "$STATE_QEMU" ]; then
  echo "FAIL[$FIXTURE]: QEMU 1 did not produce state"
  exit 1
fi

echo "[$FIXTURE 2/2 mode=$TRIGGER_MODE] vsim: resume + drain"
set +e
timeout "$TIMEOUT" "$VSIM_BIN" "$VSIM_ELF" \
  --resume-from-qemu "$STATE_QEMU" \
  --handoff-out "$STATE_VSIM" \
  --shared-mem-path "$SHARED_MEM" \
  --shared-mem-size "$SHARED_SIZE" \
  --shared-mem-base 0x00000000 \
  "${VSIM_TRIG_ARGS[@]}" \
  "${VSIM_KANATA_ARGS[@]}" </dev/null >"$SIM_LOG" 2>&1
VSIM_RC=$?
set -e

# vsim drained on the exit trigger and exited 200 (kExitHandoffToQemu).
# Anything else is a hard failure: the cycle figure is only valid when vsim
# drained cleanly.
if [ "$VSIM_RC" -ne 200 ]; then
  echo "FAIL[$FIXTURE]: vsim expected exit 200 (drain), got $VSIM_RC"
  echo "--- sim log ---"
  cat "$SIM_LOG"
  exit 1
fi

# Kernel cycles (always) + opt-in monotonic check. Offsets locked by
# state_abi_check.h (mcycle@624, minstret@632). vsim restores mcycle from
# QEMU 1's drain then counts real clock cycles, so vsim_mcycle - qemu1_mcycle
# is the measured region's cycle count. Runs before the RC gate so the
# verdict is independent of any downstream-phase failure.
read_u64_le() { od -A n -j "$1" -N 8 -t u8 "$2" | tr -d ' \n'; }
if [ -s "$STATE_VSIM" ] && [ -s "$STATE_QEMU" ]; then
  Q1_MCYCLE=$(read_u64_le 624 "$STATE_QEMU")
  Q1_MINST=$(read_u64_le  632 "$STATE_QEMU")
  V_MCYCLE=$(read_u64_le  624 "$STATE_VSIM")
  V_MINST=$(read_u64_le   632 "$STATE_VSIM")
  echo "[$FIXTURE kernel_cycles] $((V_MCYCLE - Q1_MCYCLE))  (vsim mcycle=$V_MCYCLE - qemu1 mcycle=$Q1_MCYCLE)"
  # L6: privilege survives the handoff. priv@24 locked by state_abi_check.h.
  if [ -n "${CHECK_PRIV:-}" ]; then
    Q1_PRIV=$(read_u64_le 24 "$STATE_QEMU")
    V_PRIV=$(read_u64_le  24 "$STATE_VSIM")
    echo "[$FIXTURE priv] qemu1=$Q1_PRIV vsim=$V_PRIV expected=$CHECK_PRIV"
    if [ "$Q1_PRIV" != "$CHECK_PRIV" ] || [ "$V_PRIV" != "$CHECK_PRIV" ]; then
      echo "FAIL[$FIXTURE]: drained priv mismatch (expected $CHECK_PRIV)"
      exit 1
    fi
  fi
  if [ "${CHECK_MCYCLE_MONOTONIC:-0}" = "1" ]; then
    echo "[$FIXTURE mcycle/minstret] qemu1: mcycle=$Q1_MCYCLE minstret=$Q1_MINST"
    echo "[$FIXTURE mcycle/minstret] vsim:  mcycle=$V_MCYCLE minstret=$V_MINST"
    if [ "$V_MCYCLE" -le "$Q1_MCYCLE" ]; then
      echo "FAIL[$FIXTURE]: mcycle not strictly increasing across vsim"
      exit 1
    fi
    if [ "$V_MINST" -le "$Q1_MINST" ]; then
      echo "FAIL[$FIXTURE]: minstret not strictly increasing across vsim"
      exit 1
    fi
    echo "[$FIXTURE mcycle/minstret] PASS: strictly increasing"
  fi
fi

# run --verify contract (verify_oracle F4): opt-in oracle cross-check.
#   1. hybrid marker --verify  -> oracle leg + "[verify] PASS", rc 0
#   2. hybrid pc --verify      -> same through the exit_pc oracle path
#   3. default (no --verify)   -> no verify leg, no verify output
#   4. --verify with fast/cycle -> usage error (rc 2)
#   6. run --help documents --verify
set -uo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
ROOT=$(cd -- "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/log.sh"
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/paths.sh"
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/roi.sh"

BIN="$ROOT/build/andesim"
bash "$ROOT/scripts/build_driver.sh" >/dev/null 2>&1 || fail "build_driver.sh failed"

FIXTURE="${FIXTURE:-rt_c_hello}"
hybrid_resolve_paths
ENGINE="${ENGINE:-vsim:ax45mpv_premium}"

# 1. marker mode.
OUT=$("$BIN" run --mode hybrid --trigger marker --engine "$ENGINE" --verify \
      "$VSIM_ELF" 2>&1)
RC=$?
[ "$RC" -eq 0 ] || fail "marker --verify rc=$RC: $OUT"
printf '%s\n' "$OUT" | grep -q '\[verify\] PASS' || fail "marker: no [verify] PASS: $OUT"
printf '%s\n' "$OUT" | grep -q '\[state-diff\] PASS' || fail "marker: no state-diff detail: $OUT"
printf '%s\n' "$OUT" | grep -q 'window_cycles' || fail "marker: cycle figure missing: $OUT"
ok "hybrid marker --verify: oracle cross-check PASS"

# 2. pc mode (boundaries = the fixture's own marker PCs, like docs 4.2).
OBJDUMP="${OBJDUMP:-${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN:+$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-objdump}}"
OBJDUMP="${OBJDUMP:-riscv64-unknown-elf-objdump}"
MARKERS=$(roi_markers_from_disasm "$("$OBJDUMP" -d "$VSIM_ELF")") \
  || fail "no ROI markers in $VSIM_ELF"
OUT=$("$BIN" run --mode hybrid --trigger pc --engine "$ENGINE" \
      --pc-start "0x${MARKERS%% *}" --pc-end "0x${MARKERS##* }" --verify \
      "$VSIM_ELF" 2>&1)
RC=$?
[ "$RC" -eq 0 ] || fail "pc --verify rc=$RC: $OUT"
printf '%s\n' "$OUT" | grep -q '\[verify\] PASS' || fail "pc: no [verify] PASS: $OUT"
ok "hybrid pc --verify: oracle cross-check PASS"

OUT=$("$BIN" run --mode hybrid --trigger marker --engine "$ENGINE" \
      "$VSIM_ELF" 2>&1)
RC=$?
[ "$RC" -eq 0 ] || fail "default hybrid rc=$RC: $OUT"
printf '%s\n' "$OUT" | grep -qi 'verify' && fail "default run leaked verify output: $OUT"
ok "default: verification stays off"

# 4. usage errors.
expect 2 'verify requires --mode hybrid' \
  "$BIN" run --mode fast --verify "$VSIM_ELF"
expect 2 'verify requires --mode hybrid' \
  "$BIN" run --mode cycle --verify "$VSIM_ELF"
ok "--verify usage errors (fast/cycle)"

expect 0 ' --verify ' "$BIN" run --help
ok "run --help documents --verify"

ok "run --verify oracle cross-check"
